conditions_for_special_case_citation: The legacy per-depot available CV/EV vector exactly equals a mechanically generated new level vector for that instance; equality of a rounded headline percentage is insufficient.
The same route, vehicle type, charging amount/time, demand, road, battery, charger and checker contract is retained and the saved solution passes the new cap vector.
All comparison arms use the same new fixed total and composition vector.
If only the saved solution fits but the optimized feasible set differs, cite it only as a feasible witness or legacy observation, not as an optimized result for that level.
current_special_case_assessment: No automatic special-case mapping is established. The legacy reserve-factor vector must stay labelled legacy unless the four conditions above are checked row by row.

overall_decision: Existing E4/E6 results remain valid facts for their frozen legacy constructed fleet-cap scenario, but they are not automatically any level of the new fixed-total proportion design and cannot estimate the new level effects without rerunning that design.
why_not_an_automatic_level: Legacy caps use num_cv=R_d plus additional num_ev=ceil(0.25R_d), so their total denominator exceeds the new candidate total max(R_d,R_e) in the ordinary case.
The legacy value 0.25 is a reserve factor applied to R_d, not an EV share of total fleet; rounding makes the realized cap share depot-specific.
E4 has 180/180 depot-solution EV cap hits and E6 has 1909/1920, so the changed cap changes an active feasible-set boundary rather than an idle label.

COST_PLUS_CARBON versus COST_ONLY changes route or typed path in only 2/30 paired units under the legacy cap; this is evidence of the old constrained response, not the response curve after releasing composition.
